findings.source_quote: καὶ ἣν ἔχει, μικρὰν καὶ βληχρὰν καὶ ἄνω μὴ ἔχουσαν δύναμιν.
findings.english_quote: and what he has is small and feeble and has no power to go up above[d].
findings.issue: The selected Greek describes the confession/intercession as having no power above. The English adds an action of ascending and changes the negated predicate into inability to perform that action. This does not preserve the full assertion of powerlessness above. Footnote d appropriately discloses the conjectural status of ἄνω, but that disclosure does not support adding a verb of ascent to this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “and what he has is small and feeble and has no power above[d].” Retain the disclosed working reading ἄνω and its textual note; do not substitute another witness merely because an alternative exists.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἣν ἔχει, μικρὰν καὶ βληχρὰν καὶ ἄνω μὴ ἔχουσαν δύναμιν.
findings.english_quote: What he has is small and weak, with no power to go up above[d].
findings.issue: Independently against the Greek, this clause adds ascent where the selected source states that the confession/intercession has no power above. Simplification preserves the standard edition’s altered predicate rather than the source’s negated assertion. The textual note explains the working reading above, not an additional action of going up.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “What he has is small and weak, with no power above[d].” Keep the existing disclosure that above represents the selected conjectural reading.

summary: Both editions cover all ten paragraphs and preserve the speakers, servant terminology, reciprocal work, wage, souls reading, closing promise, and selected singular understanding/service ending. Their notes distinguish editorial supplements and reported witness differences without requiring replacement of disclosed working readings. Both require correction of the added ascent in paragraph 5. This review assesses the supplied Greek and attributed edition reports; it does not authenticate unseen images or certify an exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections remain subject to fresh review.
